specification_compliance: Every product file in the diff (frame_ocr.py, models.py, database.py, indexer.py) is in the touch-point list. Core-repo changes (docs/addons/intelligence.md, the gitlink, the INDEX.md row and the spec file) are listed or implicit.

`_store_read` now receives segments and, in one session, deletes `video_frame_lines` for the file next to `video_frame_texts`, then adds the rows and writes FRAME_OCR_RULE (3). The first-read Unreadable path `_store_read(file_id, [])` therefore deletes the rows (I1, I6, item 1.4).

Segment rows are skipped with one warning naming file_id and segment.start when any line has quad None (I4). segment_index comes from enumerate over all segments, so a skipped segment leaves a gap (item 1.4).

Lines are taken from the frame that opens the segment, filtered by `box.line is not None` in the same order as the text join, so the joined lines equal segment.text (I1, I5). Reused boxes carry this frame's detected quad, because `_Box.quad` is set from this frame's detect_boxes in `_read_boxes` (I2).

A non-finite quad still fails the frame inside `_read_boxes` (`_box_rect` raises on int(round(nan)) inside the try), which agrees with the clarification. The isfinite check in `_normalised_quad` is defensive.

The migration uses CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS in `_migrate_frame_page_ocr_columns`, the same startup path as the frame OCR column migration. The model has a matching unique constraint and index name.
`_purge_file` probes for and deletes `video_frame_lines`. The only other purge callers (indexer.py:688, 3030, purge.py:61) go through `_purge_file` (I7).
`_build_rows`, `_keep_earlier_read` and `frame_read_is_outdated` are unchanged apart from the constant, so `rule < 3` is now outdated.
potential_unspecified_behavior: `_normalised_quad` is called outside the try block in `_read_video`. If a quad that `_box_rect` accepted made `np.asarray(..., dtype=float)` raise, the whole read would abort instead of failing one frame. With the current detect_boxes outputs I see no input that does this.
regression_risks: The rule bump makes every native video read at rule 2 outdated under on_index, so a large background re-read starts. This is intended (item 7) and production stays on manual until it ships.

The store deletes and re-inserts `video_frame_lines` in the same transaction as the texts. If a lines insert fails (for example the UNIQUE constraint), the whole store rolls back and the file stays pending. segment_index values are unique by construction.
test_coverage: The new 134 tests cover: one row per segment that matches its chunks; lines_json shape and non-ASCII text; join order; a segment split into several chunks; quad normalisation, corner order and clamping; dropped boxes; a reused box getting this frame's quad; a continuing frame; failed-frame numbering; three/five-point quads giving no row and one warning with unchanged text/search/flags; NaN/inf failing the frame; the store deleting stale rows; an empty read and an Unreadable first read; re-reads below rule 3; the build, rebuild-only, reindex and failed-store paths leaving rows; incomplete re-reads; the migration run twice; purging with and without the table; queue, status, details and prioritize at rule 2 versus 3; and a .loft read.

The touch point 'existing tests that seed outdated rules (NULL) also cover 2 as outdated, as an added case' is applied only in test_spec_addon_133_frame_ocr_outdated.py (the 'two' video in the not-outdated test).
